# Prior to running any code

Please download the data from https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/stefanoleone992/mutual-funds-and-etfs,
and store the file within a data/ folder in the working directory.
If the data is already stored then please skip this step.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
```

## 1. Load and clean the data

Read only the two fund files.

```{r load-data}
# Read in the dataset
etfs <- read.csv("data/ETFs.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
mutualfunds <- read.csv("data/MutualFunds.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
```

Keep the ytd return and the columns needed for the nine predictors.
Blank entries are treated as missing (`NA`).

```{r clean-data}
# Columns to keep for regression
columns <- c(
  "fund_return_ytd",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio",
  "total_net_assets",
  "inception_date",
  "asset_stocks",
  "asset_bonds",
  "annual_holdings_turnover",
  "fund_price_earning_ratio",
  "fund_sector_technology"
)

# Filter the columns but keep all rows
filtered_etfs <- etfs[, columns]
filtered_mutualfunds <- mutualfunds[, columns]

# Create indicator variable for etf and mutual fund
filtered_etfs$etf_indicator <- 1
filtered_mutualfunds$etf_indicator <- 0
funds <- rbind(filtered_etfs, filtered_mutualfunds)

# Filter for funds only created before 2021
funds <- funds %>%
  mutate(inception_date = as.Date(inception_date)) %>%
  filter(inception_date < as.Date("2021-01-01"))

# Convert running age into a continuous variable
funds$fund_age_years <- as.numeric(
  as.Date("2021-01-01") - funds$inception_date
) / 365.25

# Remove the original inception date column
funds$inception_date <- NULL

# Check missing values before excluding incomplete rows
colSums(is.na(funds))

# Keep a separate cleaned table with every model value available
model_data <- funds[complete.cases(funds), ]

# Compare counts before and after cleaning: 0 = mutual fund, 1 = ETF
table(funds$etf_indicator)
table(model_data$etf_indicator)
```

Missing stock or bond weights are **unknown, not zero**. A row missing
any required value is excluded from `model_data`, but remains in
`funds`. Recorded zeros and other non-missing values are kept. No
outliers are removed and no values are filled in. The indicator and age
are the only derived predictors; all others predictors: assets, P/E, weights, 
expenses, turnover, and returns are unchanged.

## 2. Fit the model

```{r regression}
model <- lm(
  fund_return_ytd ~ total_net_assets +
    fund_age_years + asset_stocks + asset_bonds +
    annual_holdings_turnover + fund_price_earning_ratio +
    fund_sector_technology +
    fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio * etf_indicator,
  data = model_data
)
```

The ETF coefficient compares ETFs with mutual funds while holding the
other predictors fixed. No transformations or corrections are applied to
this model.

## 3. Summary tables and tests

```{r}
# Describe fitted model
summary(model)
```
```{r}
# Describe cleaned dataset including potentially unused observations
summary(model_data)
```

```{r}
# The response and predictors for the exact observations
# used within the regression
summary(model.frame(model))
```

```{r design-matrix}
# Design matrix
X <- model.matrix(model)

# Standardized third moment: positive = right skew,
# negative = left skew. Undefined for constant columns
skewness <- function(x) {
  spread <- sqrt(mean((x - mean(x))^2))
  if (spread == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  mean(((x - mean(x)) / spread)^3)
}

design_summary <- X[, colnames(X) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value),
    median = median(value),
    SD = sd(value),
    min = min(value),
    max = max(value),
    skewness = skewness(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(design_summary, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# 95% confidence interval
confint(model)
```

```{r}
# ANOVA test
intercept_only <- lm(fund_return_ytd ~ 1, data = model_data)
anova(intercept_only, model)
```

```{r}
# Test each predictor while accounting for all the others
drop1(model, test = "F")
```

```{r}
# The first column is the response; exclude it from predictor covariance
covariance_matrix <- cov(model_data[, -1])
knitr::kable(signif(covariance_matrix, 4))
```

The covariance diagonal runs from top left to bottom right and contains
variances. Covariances depend on units, so their sizes alone do not
measure collinearity. Four significant digits are used only to display
the table.

## 4. Graphs

These plots use the original returns and ordinary residuals. A residual
is observed return minus fitted return; calculating it does not
transform the model.

**Boxplot:** compare returns between ETFs and mutual funds.

```{r return-boxplot}
boxplot(fund_return_ytd ~ etf_indicator,
  data = model_data,
  names = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"),
  ylab = "2021 (Jan-Nov) returns (decimal)", 
  main = "2021 (Jan-Nov) returns by fund type"
)
```

**Histogram:** examine the distribution of returns.

```{r return-histogram}
hist(model_data$fund_return_ytd,
  xlab = "2021 (Jan-Nov) returns (decimal)", 
  main = "Distribution of 2021 (Jan-Nov) returns"
)
```

**Residual plot:** 

```{r residual-plot}
plot(fitted(model), residuals(model),
  xlab = "Fitted return", ylab = "Residual", main = "Residuals versus fitted"
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```

**Residual vs response per perdictor** Large individual graphs

```{r predictor-residuals, fig.width=10, fig.height=18}
predictor_data <- as.data.frame(
  model.matrix(model)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
)

# Five rows and two columns provide space for nine plots.
par(mfrow = c(5, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

for (predictor in names(predictor_data)) {
  plot(
    predictor_data[[predictor]],
    residuals(model),
    xlab = predictor,
    ylab = "Residual",
    pch = 20,
    cex.lab = 0.8
  )
  abline(h = 0, col = "red")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Residuals for predictor:** Matrix format

```{r residual-pairs, fig.width=16, fig.height=16}
# Get all model terms, including the interaction, without the intercept
plot_data <- as.data.frame(
  model.matrix(model)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
)

# Add residuals as the last column
plot_data$Residuals <- residuals(model)

# Match short labels to the actual column names
short_labels <- c(
  total_net_assets = "Assets",
  fund_age_years = "Age",
  asset_stocks = "Stocks",
  asset_bonds = "Bonds",
  annual_holdings_turnover = "Turnover",
  fund_price_earning_ratio = "P/E",
  fund_sector_technology = "Technology",
  fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio = "Expense",
  etf_indicator = "ETF",
  "fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio:etf_indicator" = "Expense × ETF",
  "etf_indicator:fund_annual_report_net_expense_ratio" = "Expense × ETF",
  Residuals = "Residuals"
)

# Keep original names if a column has no matching short label
labels <- names(plot_data)
matched <- labels %in% names(short_labels)
labels[matched] <- unname(short_labels[labels[matched]])

pairs(
  plot_data,
  labels = labels,
  pch = 1,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = adjustcolor("black", alpha.f = 0.3),
  main = "Predictors, interaction, and residuals",
  panel = function(x, y, ...) {
    points(x, y, ...)

    # Residuals on the vertical axis: horizontal zero line
    if (par("mfg")[1] == ncol(plot_data)) {
      abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
    }

    # Residuals on the horizontal axis: vertical zero line
    if (par("mfg")[2] == ncol(plot_data)) {
      abline(v = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
    }
  }
)
```

**Normal Q-Q plot:**

```{r qq-plot}
qqnorm(residuals(model), main = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals")
qqline(residuals(model), col = "red")
```

**Residual boxplot:** to compare the spread of errors between fund types

```{r residual-boxplot}
boxplot(residuals(model) ~ model_data$etf_indicator,
  names = c("Mutual fund", "ETF"),
  ylab = "Residual", xlab = "Etf Indicator",
  main = "Residuals by fund type"
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```
